- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (-1.00) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow slight lag or mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast peak at 1–2 days after spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for final 10–15 days of horizon.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes — introduce slight volatility bump in forecast to reflect sentiment inertia.  
- Model often lags 1–2 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for sentiment-driven corrections.
